newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AROMA SLIDES AFTER CAUTIONARY ON BUY-OUT.
newsitem.headline: AROMA SLIDES AFTER CAUTIONARY ON BUY-OUT.

text.p: Aroma Liquor Holdings Ltd slumped on Monday after issuing a cautionary that a controlling interest in the company would be sold at a substantial discount to Friday's closing price of 224 cents per share.
The share was last down 58 cents, or 25.89 percent, to 164 rand in thin volumes of 14,700 valued at over 30,000 rand.
"The share could be down on the listing of Rebhold on Wednesday but definitely it is down on the cautionary," a dealer said.

Liquor, food and freight forwarding company Rebhold will list on the Johannesbug Stock Exchange on Wednesday and plans to raise about 50 million rand through the issue of 23 million shares at 220 cents in a private share placing.
An analyst who asked not to be identified said that Rebhold was known to be in the market for acquisitions and one of them could be Aroma.
"Rebhold has said it was in line for two acquisitions. I would not be surprised if Aroma were the other party," he said.
He said Aroma had been struggling particularly in the Western Cape market.
Aroma issued a cautionary on October 7 that it was in talks and its share price rallied to 224 cents by last Friday, twice its price on October 7.
Analysts attributed the rise to speculation.
"Aroma is not a liquid share. The family holds a majority of the stocks. The price rise was a speculative drive," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
